title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?
summary:

title: Ken Griffin calls Trump’s tariffs on US allies 'a disaster' and predicts it will hurt Republicans in the midterms
summary:
Ken Griffin sees trouble ahead for Republicans and says Donald Trump’s fights with America’s allies are part of the problem.
“I think that the tariff battles with Canada, with Europe, with our allies has just been a disaster,” Griffin said.
Griffin predicted Republicans would almost certainly lose control of at least one chamber of Congress, describing the midterms as a check on the party in power.
“The House almost is in a really tough spot and the Senate's going to be really close," Griffin said.
Griffin also has thoughts on Trump’s explanation of the war in Iran and called the administration’s treatment of immigrants "disgraceful."

title: Trump announces $8 billion for farmers to offset soaring diesel costs
summary:
President Trump announced an $8 billion aid package on Monday to help US farmers pay for diesel this harvest season.
The relief program, announced at a campaign rally in Kansas and on social media, aims to bring down fuel costs for Americans ahead of next month's midterm elections.
"Tonight, I am also pleased to announce that the Department of Agriculture will be launching a new 'Harvest Fuel Relief Program,' providing our Farmers with 8 BILLION DOLLARS in support to offset Diesel costs during this Harvest Season," Trump's account posted on Truth Social (DJT).
(Photo by DUSTIN FRANZ / AFP via Getty Images) · DUSTIN FRANZ via Getty ImagesThe Harvest Fuel Relief Program will be administered by the US Department of Agriculture.
Earlier this month, the Trump administration moved to lift restrictions on red-dyed diesel, a tax-exempt fuel typically reserved for tractors and farm gear.

title: Homebuyers are canceling sales at near-record rates
summary:
Homebuyers are backing out of contracts at near-record rates, a potential sign of how higher mortgage rates are prompting buyers to rethink their plans.
But pending sales tend to fall through at higher rates when buyers have more options and more negotiating power, as they currently do in much of the country.
Indeed, metro areas that are notably buyer's markets, like Jacksonville and Tampa, Fla., and Las Vegas, all had contract cancellation rates approaching 20%, higher than anywhere else in the country.
But they're relatively rare in strong seller's markets like San Francisco, where just 2.8% of deals fell apart.
Claire Boston is a Senior Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

title: Housing Market Warning: Homebuilder Sentiment Drops to 14-Year Low
summary:
Homebuilder sentiment fell three points to 29 in October, according to the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index.
October's reading marks the lowest homebuilder sentiment the US has seen since June 2012, the NAHB said, when the housing market was still moving through the aftermath of the 2008 crisis.
